intent: The native radio or checkbox input of a QuestionnaireChoice, invisible and stretched over the whole row so the row is its click target.
typical_uses: The input a QuestionnaireChoice renders for itself

dont_use_when.situation: Adding an answer to a question

invariants.text: Its `checked`, `name`, `type`, `value`, `disabled` and `required` come from the enclosing QuestionnaireChoice and its item, which is why its props omit them; the name is dropped while the item is skipped, so a skipped item submits nothing.
QuestionnaireChoice renders one QuestionnaireChoiceInput itself and is the only provider of the context this part needs, so a consumer-placed one always lands beside that built-in input.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a QuestionnaireChoiceInput to build a custom choice layout
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use QuestionnaireChoice and restyle it through questionnaire.module.css; this part throws outside a QuestionnaireChoice, and inside one it adds a second input to the row

a11y.by: questionnaire.test.tsx asserts the input found by role radio has type "radio", and the one found by role checkbox in a multiple item has type "checkbox"

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the input's own state (`QuestionnaireChoiceState`: checked, disabled, invalid, shortcut, type), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.

good.title: The input comes with the choice

bad.title: A second input inside a choice
bad.why: The row already renders its input; the nested one is a second native radio with the same name and value inside the label.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<QuestionnaireChoiceState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the input's own state (`QuestionnaireChoiceState`: checked, disabled, invalid, shortcut, type), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.
